deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two short memoranda of observational and instrumental data. It contains no mathematical derivation.

(A) 'Radien der Linsenflächen am Objectiv des Passageinstruments' (radii of the lens surfaces of the objective of the transit instrument). Four numbers are listed: R1 = 1430.291, R2 = 582.818, R3 = -585.231, R4 = 2113.524. A small mark above the first number may indicate the unit. These are presumably the four surface radii of a cemented or air-spaced two-lens achromat, in order from front to back. Only R3 carries an explicit sign. The page gives no unit, no sign convention, no refractive indices and no thicknesses, so the focal length cannot be reconstructed from it.
- Plausible reading: a crown lens (R1, R2) followed by a flint lens (R3, R4). The near-equality |R2| ≈ |R3| (582.8 vs 585.2) suggests the inner surfaces nearly match.
- This is a record of data only; no calculation is made.

(B) 'Rumpfsches Barometer' (barometer by the Göttingen mechanic Rumpf). Readings are in Paris inches and lines, with attached thermometer in degrees Celsius ('Th Cent'). In the original, the inch and line units are marked by small superscripts ('26 ² 9 ¹ 80').
- 1849 Dec 27, 10h a.m.: 26 in 9.80 lines (= 321.80 lines), thermometer +0.7 °C.
- 1850 Jan 22, 8¼h a.m. (8 corrected to 8¼): 28 in 1.77 lines (= 337.77 lines), thermometer -8.4 °C (a '+' struck out).
- 'Gleich darauf unten nachgeschraubt, was seit 1849 Dec. 27 absichtlich unterlassen war' (immediately afterwards the screw at the bottom was readjusted, which had been deliberately omitted since Dec 27): 28 in 2.33 lines. The screw presumably sets the cistern mercury level to the fiducial zero, as in a Fortin-type barometer.
- Jan 22 effect of the readjustment (my computation): +0.56 lines (≈ +1.26 mm).
- 1850 Jan 26, 3¼h p.m.: 26 in 9.30 lines, thermometer 0.00 °C. After screwing below: 26 in 8.90 lines. Effect (my computation): -0.40 lines (≈ -0.90 mm).
- Apparent purpose: to test how far neglecting the cistern adjustment over about a month biases the readings.
- Converted at 1 Paris line = 2.25583 mm (my computation): 725.9, 761.9, 763.2, 724.8 and 723.9 mm.
- No reduction to 0 °C is performed on the page.
errors: No errors are detectable. The page is raw data without computation.
The roughly 36 mm swing between Dec 27 and Jan 22 is large but meteorologically plausible: a strong cold anticyclone at -8.4 °C.

transcription_corrections: The units in the barometer readings appear as small superscripts in the original ('26 ² 9 ¹ 80'), marking Paris inches and lines; the transcription's ″ and ′ are an interpretation of these marks.
Jan 22 time: an '8' was overwritten or corrected to '8¼' and the struck-out sign before 8.4 is '+'; the value is -8.4 °C. The transcription has this right.
A small mark above '1430,291' (possibly a unit sign) is omitted in the transcription.
'Gleich darauf': the word written above, possibly a corrected 'Zu…', is illegible; the reading 'unten nachgeschraubt' is supported by the later 'nachdem unten geschr.'
